card.name: News health-study headline and lead words
card.fires_on: Words in the opening lines of news-style science and health stories, such as a verb, dash, comma or linking word right after the subject of a study finding. It is strongest where the sentence is about to state what research found.

modes.label: Study-finding lead
modes.description: A verb, comma, dash or conjunction after the subject in a lead sentence reporting new research.
modes.example: HAVING siblings and a pet dog that comes inside the home can protect infants from developing egg allergies by age one<<,>> new research has shown.

modes.label: Headline word
modes.description: A key word in a short health news headline, often before the dateline.
modes.example: Insomnia Might Boost Heart Failure<< Risk>> WEDNESDAY, March

modes.label: Dateline or attribution
modes.description: A state abbreviation or reporting verb in a news attribution.
modes.example: according to project manager John Gerpheide of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Pasadena,<< Calif>>.

card.writes: It seems to lower the odds of Chinese news-attribution phrases like 'according to reporters', and nudges toward a few odd word pieces.
card.plain: It fires in the first sentences of news reports about health studies, as the sentence heads toward what the research showed.
